newsitem.title: INDIA: India L&T 1996/97 order book up 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: India L&T 1996/97 order book up 22 pct.

text.p: Indian engineering and construction firm Larsen & Toubro said it booked orders worth 56.38 billion rupees during 1996/97 (April-March), representing a 22 percent increase over the previous year.
It said its cement output rose to 5.4 million tonnes during the year from 3.8 million tonnes in 1995/96.

"However, due to the perceptible slowdown in construction activities from the later half of 1996/97, low investment in infrastructure areas and overall slowing down of the economy, cement prices were very depressed," Larsen said.
Higher manufacturing cost due to increases in prices of power, coal and freight had a "substantial adverse impact on margins," the company said in a statement.
Major orders booked during the year included 3.41 billion rupee process platform for Oil and Natural Gas Corp and a 3.0 billion construction project for Reliance Petroleum, it said.
"The slowing down of the Indian economy during the second half of 1996/97 had resulted in lower order booking during that period," the company said.

"It is expected that the bold initiatives announced by the finance minister in the 1997/98 budget and the pragmatic slack season credit policy announced by the Reserve Bank of India will provide the necessary fillip to the economy which will in turn result in investments in the core sector," it said.
"The company therefore expects a significant pickup in order booking in the second half of 1997/98," it said.
It said L&T received a letter of intent from Haldia Petrochemicals Ltd for building a captive power plant on a build, operate and own basis.
